Phase 2 (Late Ottoman, c. 1885): five partly hewn, partly built plastered cisterns, the chamber used by masons and as a refuse pit, the cave rebuilt and blocked (reuse rows coded separately).

title: Jerusalem, Robinson’s Arch

location_note: Below the paved street at Robinson's Arch, southwestern corner of the Temple Mount, Old City of Jerusalem; no map reference in the report
notes: Cleaning and excavation of the northernmost c. 120 m of the large drainage channel (first exposed by Warren 1867): built and slab-covered to the south, rock-hewn with an elongated vault around the Temple Mount corner, quarried in the Herodian expansion (excavators' relative phase 5). Pre-expansion dwelling remains: a stepped unplastered cavity (excavators: not a miqveh), a vaulted rock-hewn room, and a Second Temple miqveh that postdates the room's opening. A circular cistern crossed by the channel is dated by its clay plaster to Iron II. Other segments of the same channel in other reports (e.g. HAESI-26183) are separate reports of the same structure.

title: Jerusalem, Jerusalem Forest
author: David Tanami
notes: Nahal Ravida near Nahal Soreq: an arcosolium burial cave (Byzantine by plan; robbed), later a limekiln before its entrance (not a class) and then probable storage or dwelling use (undated); beam-and-weight Winepresses 1 and 3 ascribed to Iron Age II, the collecting vat of Winepress 1 converted to a modern cement-coated cistern; a simple Winepress 2 and an unexplained rock-cut installation L401, undated. Only non-diagnostic sherds.
